# The Hollins Lane orchard, autumn notes

Mara Okafor, who has kept the Hollins Lane orchard since 2019, says the old
Bramley by the gate is the oldest tree on the lane. The parish records do not
say when it was planted, so that is hearsay for now.

Every apple tree needs a second variety nearby to set fruit. That is not a
local quirk; it is how apples pollinate, and the nursery leaflet says the same.

This year the orchard pressed 140 litres of juice, up from 90 last year. I
counted the bottles myself on 12 October.

The rise came after the volunteers spread leaf mould under the trees in March.
Mara thinks the mulch made the difference. I am less sure: a warm, wet spring
would explain most of it, and every orchard in the valley did well.

The parish council's grounds team wants to mow the meadow strip in July.
Mowing then would cut the wildflowers before they seed, and the strip exists
to feed the pollinators the orchard depends on. If the strip is mown in July,
the orchard loses the very insects that set its fruit.

We agreed to ask the council to wait until September. Mara will write the
letter; I will bring the bottle count as evidence.

Open question: does the lease let the parish mow without asking us?
